title: API Reliability and Observability Engineering
stage: Observe, diagnose, contain, and recover the promise
centralQuestion: How do operators know whether the user promise is still true, and how do they recover it without making the incident worse?
responsibility: Make failures observable and recoverable through explicit budgets, lifecycle states, telemetry meaning, service-level objectives, fault experiments, and reconciliation.
incomingBoundary: The Course 3 API 1.2 service protected by Security Profile 1.0 and migrations 001–007.
outgoingBoundary: Reliability Profile 1.0, migration 008, critical journeys, deadline and resilience policies, lifecycle controls, telemetry contracts, SLOs, alerts, runbooks, game-day evidence, and reconciliation plans.
versionState: API 1.2 and Security Profile 1.0 preserved; Reliability Profile 1.0 introduced; migrations 001–008.
languageStrategy: one primary implementation track plus one comparative reference track

modules.title: Reliability Model and Critical Journeys
modules.centralQuestion: Which user journeys matter, what makes them good or bad, and which durable facts establish the outcome?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Create the reliability case, critical-journey populations, failure modes, ownership, residual risk, and negative claims.
learningOutcomes: Define critical journeys and eligible event populations
Separate prevention, mitigation, repair, and verification
Choose public or durable correctness oracles before telemetry
Catalog failure modes and residual risks
Trace reliability requirements to tests, runbooks, and owners

modules.title: Deadlines, Cancellation, and Retry Budgets
modules.centralQuestion: How is one absolute time budget propagated through retries, dependencies, and cancellation without multiplying work?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Implement monotonic deadlines, child budgets, safe retry classification, backoff, Retry-After handling, and cancellation.
learningOutcomes: Distinguish absolute deadlines from per-call timeouts
Budget connect, pool, transaction, read, write, and cleanup waits
Preserve committed durable work after caller cancellation
Retry only safe or idempotent effects
Use bounded backoff, jitter, and `Retry-After` inside the remaining budget

modules.title: Dependency Resilience and Graceful Degradation
modules.centralQuestion: How should circuits, bulkheads, and degradation be scoped so they contain rather than hide dependency failure?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Add dependency-local state machines, bounded probes, concurrency isolation, and truthful degraded responses.
learningOutcomes: Classify dependency failures and ownership
Use bulkheads to bound local resource consumption
Design circuit state and half-open probe ownership
Avoid fallbacks that fabricate correctness
Keep telemetry failure from becoming business failure

modules.title: Lifecycle, Health, Shutdown, and Recovery
modules.centralQuestion: How do APIs, workers, and dispatchers start, become ready, drain, stop, and recover without losing accepted work?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Implement lifecycle states, liveness/readiness separation, graceful draining, lease handling, and startup reconciliation.
learningOutcomes: Separate startup, liveness, and readiness
Stop accepting before draining
Bound graceful shutdown and preserve durable claims
Recover incomplete work on startup
Make health endpoints report service ability, not every dependency detail

modules.title: Telemetry Architecture and Structured Events
modules.centralQuestion: Which operational events are useful, bounded, redacted, versioned, and clearly separated from business truth?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Create the telemetry vocabulary, correlation rules, bounded sinks, exporter failure behavior, and privacy policy.
learningOutcomes: Separate logs, metrics, traces, and audit records by purpose
Use stable event names and fields
Propagate correlation and trace context safely
Bound queues and drop behavior
Treat telemetry as evidence about execution, not the authority on durable state

modules.title: Metrics and Service-Level Indicators
modules.centralQuestion: How are counters, gauges, histograms, and SLI populations defined so the math means what operators think it means?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Implement bounded metric dimensions, units, good/bad/eligible/excluded populations, and aggregation semantics.
learningOutcomes: Choose metric instruments from the measured quantity
Control label dimensions and series count
Measure latency distributions rather than averages
Define good, bad, eligible, and excluded events
Use durable timestamps for asynchronous journey indicators

modules.title: Distributed Tracing Across Asynchronous Work
modules.centralQuestion: How does trace context cross HTTP, queues, workers, storage, retries, and webhooks without inventing false parentage?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Implement validated context, synchronous parent-child spans, asynchronous links, attempts, queue time, and privacy-safe attributes.
learningOutcomes: Parse and validate W3C trace context
Create bounded span names and attributes
Represent queue and worker attempts accurately
Link asynchronous work to durable causation
Understand sampling and missing-span limits

modules.title: SLOs, Error Budgets, Dashboards, and Alerts
modules.centralQuestion: How do versioned SLOs, exact error budgets, burn rates, dashboards, alerts, and runbooks drive decisions?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Publish five journey SLOs, multiwindow alerts, owner-linked runbooks, and release policy.
learningOutcomes: Choose objectives from critical journeys
Calculate compliance and remaining error budget
Use multiwindow burn-rate alerts
Design dashboards from outcomes to causes
Handle insufficient data and planned exclusions explicitly

modules.title: Fault Injection, Troubleshooting, and Game Days
modules.centralQuestion: How can fault injection and game days produce falsifiable evidence without creating uncontrolled damage?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Design bounded faults, control populations, abort conditions, cleanup contracts, and proof-sensitive planted defects.
learningOutcomes: Predict the failure and first oracle before injection
Control blast radius and synthetic tenants
Diagnose from user journey to durable state to telemetry
Prove alerts and runbooks are sensitive to planted defects
Verify cleanup mechanically

modules.title: Incident Command, Reconciliation, and Readiness
modules.centralQuestion: How do responders command an incident, reconcile durable state, repair safely, and decide whether a release is operationally ready?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Run incident roles, read-only reconciliation, stable repair plans, verification, retrospective, and observable release gates.
learningOutcomes: Assign incident command, operations, communication, and recording roles
Construct a timeline with source and confidence
Reconcile database, jobs, artifacts, and outbox state
Generate stable repair actions before mutation
Close only after user outcomes, cleanup, and regressions are verified
